reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's concern for the Hebrew people's welfare. God states: 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people...and have heard their cry...I know their sufferings' (the passage contains 'צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָה אֵלַי' - the cry of Israel has come to me, and 'רָאִיתִי אֶת־ הַלַּחַץ אֲשֶׁר מִצְרַיִם לֹחֲצִים אֹתָם' - I have seen the oppression). God then actively intervenes by sending Moses to Pharaoh with the explicit mission: 'הוֹצֵא אֶת־ עַמִּי בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרָֽיִם' - to bring out His people from Egypt. This passage from the burning bush theophany demonstrates God's recognition of suffering, compassionate response, and concrete plan for deliverance—all of which affirm God's desire for the people's well-being.
